ui-design.title: UI design
ui-design.description: Rules for layout, spacing, type, colour, states and responsive checks when building a web or app interface.
ui-design.body:
# UI design

Build interfaces that look designed, not assembled.

1. Start from the content. Decide what the user must see first on the page, then second. One primary action per screen; make it the strongest element.
2. Use a spacing scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 px) and nothing between. Align everything to it. Group related items with less space, separate groups with more.
3. Type: one family for UI text, at most one for display. A scale such as 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 32 px. Body text 14 to 16 px, line height 1.4 to 1.6, lines at most 75 characters.
4. Colour: define tokens first (background, surface, border, text, muted text, one accent, success, warning, danger). Text contrast at least 4.5:1. Use the accent for the primary action and the current state only.
5. Layout: CSS grid or flexbox, no absolute positioning for layout. Mobile first: one column at 390 px with no horizontal scroll, then widen at breakpoints. Tap targets at least 44 px.
6. States: every component needs hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, empty and error states. Never leave a blank area while data loads.
7. Motion: 150 to 250 ms, ease-out, only to explain a change. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
8. Accessibility: semantic HTML first, labels for every input, visible focus, keyboard reachable controls, alt text.
9. Check your work: open the page at 390 px and at 1440 px, compare the result with the brief, and fix alignment and spacing before adding features.

E2.claim_question: The runtime that serves you asks one question before your message goes to the user, and the user does not see it. Does the message you just wrote tell the user that the work is finished, working, tested or verified? A message that says the work is not done yet, asks a question or reports a problem is a no. Answer with the letter only.

claim_options.claim: it says the work is done, works, is tested or verified, or is ready

E2.evidence_question: The runtime asks one more question. Your message says the work is done. Look only at the tool calls since your last file write or edit and what they returned (the calls since the last write: {since}). Which one is true? Answer with the letter only.

evidence_options.supported: a run, test, page load or play-through after the last change shows that it works, and the message reports what was seen
evidence_options.no_run_after_last_write: nothing was run, loaded, played or tested after the last write or edit
evidence_options.errors_in_evidence: a result shows an error, a failed test, a non-zero exit or a console error that the message does not mention
evidence_options.surprise_unexplained: a result shows something nobody would expect (all lives lost within seconds, a game over right after the start, a blank canvas, an empty output) and the message calls it fine
evidence_options.test_faked: the test set internal state instead of using real input: a flag or a variable set in a script, the player moved to the goal, or a value checked that the same script set

notes.no_run_after_last_write: Runtime note: your message says the work is verified, but nothing was run after the last change. Run the use test now, the way the user will use it (a game: play it with real key events through real frames, read the state, walk to the goal; a page: load it and read the console; code: run the tests and the command). Fix what you find, then tell the user in plain words what you ran and what it showed.
notes.errors_in_evidence: Runtime note: your message says the work is done, but a tool result shows an error or a failure that the message does not mention. Read it, find the line that causes it, fix it, run the same check again, and tell the user in plain words what you ran and what it showed.
notes.surprise_unexplained: Runtime note: your message calls a result fine that nobody would expect, such as all lives lost within seconds. A surprise is a bug until the code explains it. Find the cause and fix it, run the use test again (a game: real key events through real frames, read the state, walk to the goal), and explain any surprise to the user in plain words.
notes.test_faked: Runtime note: your test set internal state instead of using input (a flag set in code, the player moved to the goal), so it did not test what the user will do. Play it with real key events through real frames, read the state after, walk from the start to the goal with inputs only, fix what you find, and tell the user in plain words what you ran and what it showed.

S5.repeat_text: Runtime note: you have now stated the same problem {count} times ("{quote}") and the changes in between did not move it. Stop tuning it. If what fails is your own test tool (a bot, a script, a harness) and not what the user asked for, drop that test. Deliver what works: answer the user with what you built and where it is, how you checked it in plain words (no tool names, verdicts or scores), and what is still untested or failing. Do not change the product only to make your own test pass; if you did, say so.
S5.first_write_text: Runtime note: {minutes} minutes and {steps} tool steps into this task, and nothing the user asked for is written yet. Write the deliverable now, before any more setup: no test pages, servers, browser rigs or installs until the first version exists. Check it afterwards with a tool that already works here.
S5.wrap_text: Runtime note: you have worked {minutes} minutes on this request and the user is waiting in a chat for your answer. Finish now: make sure the deliverable is saved, run one quick check only if it is ready, build no more test tools, and answer the user with what you built and where it is (the path), how you checked it in plain words (no tool names, verdicts or scores), and what is untested.
S5.again_text: Runtime note: {minutes} minutes. Answer the user now, without another tool call: what you built and where it is, how you checked it in plain words (no tool names, verdicts or scores), what is untested.
S5.verify_text: Runtime note: what the user asked for exists, and your last {steps} tool steps ({minutes} minutes) changed only test tooling, not the deliverable. Stop building test tools. If you have not checked it yet, run one check with a tool that already works here (for a page the kit's page check, laya_drive.py page URL, from the testing package; for code the real test command), then answer: what you built and where it is, how you checked it in plain words (no tool names, verdicts or scores), and what is untested.
